summary: An empty peer card is now counted as an empty peer card, not reported as a failed read.
details: nora_peer_card_empty_total was incremented by nora/engagement/context.py but never declared in nora/obs/metric_specs.py, so Metrics.inc fell past its counter branch to a bare self._gauges[name] lookup and raised KeyError. That raise happens inside _peer_card's own `except Exception`, which logs 'peer-card read failed' and increments nora_errors_total{stage="peer_card"} - so the one counter whose purpose is to separate 'her card is genuinely empty' from 'the read failed' reported every genuinely empty card as a transport failure. Inverted, not merely missing.
Confirmed against the running container before the fix: the series was absent from /metrics entirely while the code that writes it runs on every tagged turn.

The instance was one line. The defect was that nothing compared call sites against the declaration tuple, so tests/architecture/test_every_recorded_metric_is_declared.py now does - resolving string literals, module-level constants and conditionals over them (132 distinct names across 204 call sites, including the private _inc/_gauge forwarding wrappers where the unchecked name was hiding).
limitations: The gate reads metric names statically. A call site whose name it cannot resolve - a forwarding wrapper taking `name` as a parameter - is pinned in an explicit allowlist rather than skipped, so a NEW unresolvable site fails the gate instead of passing it unchecked. A genuinely computed metric name still cannot be checked statically and would need a runtime assertion.

The gate checks metric NAMES only, not labels. Metrics._full_labels defaults a missing label to "" and silently drops an undeclared one, so a call site passing a label the spec does not declare is still unreported.
